title: Rotate JWT Signing Keys
content:
Runbook: Rotate JWT Signing Keys

When to Use This

Use this runbook when:

  • A signing key has been compromised or suspected compromised
  • Scheduled key rotation (every 90 days)
  • Recovering from a signing key leak in logs

⚠️ This will invalidate all active sessions. Users will be forced to log in again.

Prerequisites

  • AWS CLI configured with prod profile
  • Access to auth-service Kubernetes namespace
  • kubectl configured for prod cluster
  • PagerDuty incident opened (for compromise scenarios)
  • Approval from team lead (for scheduled rotations)

Steps

1. Generate New Key Pair

# Generate RSA-4096 private key
openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:4096   -out new_private_key.pem

# Extract public key
openssl rsa -pubout -in new_private_key.pem -out new_public_key.pem

# Verify
openssl rsa -in new_private_key.pem -check

Expected output: RSA key ok

2. Upload to AWS Secrets Manager

# Upload private key
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value \
  --profile prod \
  --secret-id auth/jwt/signing-key \
  --secret-string "$(cat new_private_key.pem)"

# Upload public key (for verifier services)
aws secretsmanager put-secret-value \
  --profile prod \
  --secret-id auth/jwt/verification-key \
  --secret-string "$(cat new_public_key.pem)"

3. Rolling Restart auth-service

kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service -n auth
kubectl rollout status deployment/auth-service -n auth

Wait for: deployment "auth-service" successfully rolled out

4. Verify New Key Is Active

# Get a fresh token and decode header
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST https://auth.internal/login \
  -d '{"email":"test@internal","password":"test"}' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" | jq -r .access_token)

# Decode header (kid should match new key)
echo $TOKEN | cut -d. -f1 | base64 -d | jq .

5. Invalidate All Active Sessions

# This purges the token family table — ALL users will be logged out
kubectl exec -it deploy/auth-service -n auth -- \
  auth-service admin purge-sessions --confirm

6. Notify Stakeholders

  • Post in #engineering-alerts: "JWT signing key rotation complete. All users will need to log in again."
  • Update PagerDuty incident (if applicable)
  • Log rotation in the security changelog

Rollback

If issues arise after restart:

# Restore previous key version
aws secretsmanager restore-secret-version \
  --profile prod \
  --secret-id auth/jwt/signing-key \
  --version-stage AWSPREVIOUS

kubectl rollout undo deployment/auth-service -n auth
kubectl rollout status deployment/auth-service -n auth

Verification

After rollback, confirm the old kid is back in token headers.

Check error rates in Grafana: Auth Service Dashboard
